law: Ordinary count under not-all-equal, simultaneous rounds, no extra takes, no short members.
scope: Three additional connected starts of dimension two; all ten pairs of five such starts. Two nonisomorphic five-knot rings with the same proved exponential rate and the recorded pair of bare rings.
selection: The longer bare row exercises a relay. The four-ring repeats the ends of the three-knot row. The six-ring was chosen to put a repeating pair beside a relay. The two five-rings differ only in whether their knots keeping leftovers meet.

sources.dimension of the rows: proofs/RELAY-IDENT-20261119-001A/RELAY-IDENT-20261119-001A-P001_relays/proof.md, Theorem 5, Corollary 6 and validation for the row of seven; research/CHAIN-IDENT-20261119-001/chain_ident.md, The dimension.
sources.dimension of the four-ring: Direct reduction. Each opposite pair joins through its two common knots and each of its members has two loose distinctions. An isolated knot with two loose distinctions makes exactly such a pair after one round. Thus each part is one round further along the same relay as a part of the two-touching start. They remain separate because each new knot meets only its parents among the old knots. The two parts each make t+2 births in round t.
sources.dimension of the six-ring: Direct reduction using the alternating groups of three in research/BREAK-EDDIES-20261119-001/break_eddies.md and the relay in proofs/RELAY-IDENT-20261119-001A/RELAY-IDENT-20261119-001A-P001_relays/proof.md, Theorem 4, step 4. After round 1 one part is an isolated knot with one loose distinction; it makes k births in its kth later round. In the other part a join and an offshoot meet a common parent and hold one and two loose distinctions respectively. Each subsequent round makes one join of both and one offshoot of the second; these meet through that same second parent, so their holdings are again one and two. In round t >= 2 the count is (t-1)+2 = t+1. Within the repeating part the join with one fresh distinction persists in every round.
sources.two touching knots: No common knot joins the two starts. Each separately makes two offshoots; from there each part is the preceding proof's relay shifted by one round. Every join of that relay has two parents and two fresh distinctions. Thus the six-ring carries a local kind absent from the two touching knots at every t >= 2.
sources.equal ring rate: research/RING-CORES-20261119-001/ring_cores.md, Theorems 3 and 4; publication/knotlab/INTUITIONS.md, lesson 8.7, A dial. Each five-ring has lap weight y^5(1+y)^2 and exponential rate the positive root of x^7=(x+1)^2, about 1.2628. Whether the two knots keeping a leftover meet distinguishes the starts under renaming. The rate theorem gives no identity of either local reading.

same-rate rings beyond the checked round.evidence: A deduction from the ring theorems after the finite comparison. All seven instances through round 32 were also counted. This deduction concerns t = 5l+1 for all integers l >= 0.

argument: A birth of round t is a cluster of size t+1, a consecutive run of ring members in join order (two steps around the five-ring), together with selected members for leftover distinctions. If the run has M available leftover members and a are selected, there are 2+M-a possible additions, the two ends and the available leftovers. This is its fresh count.
At t = 5l+1 the cluster has size 5l+2. If a >= 1 its run has length at most 5l+1, with M <= 2l+1 since each period of five carries two leftovers. Its fresh count is at most 2l+2.

If a = 0 there are five runs of length 5l+2. Each has two parents, from deleting either end, and its leftover count is 2l plus the number in a consecutive pair after l full periods. Two knots adjacent in the start are nonadjacent in join order, and conversely.

With the originally adjacent knots the five pairs contain one leftover four times and two zero times. With the originally nonadjacent knots the corresponding counts are two and one. Thus the numbers of two-parent joins with 2l+3 fresh distinguish the rings in one direction (4 versus 2), and those with 2l+4 fresh distinguish them in the other (0 versus 1). They force damage above the count gap on all these rounds. Every match under sig1 also matches under sig0, so this holds for both readings.

comparison columns: total variation with uniform weight per birth
comparison meaning: Damage above the absolute count gap is twice the smaller unmatched count. A positive value means the count difference alone cannot explain the local damage. Total variation compares normalized local-kind counts exactly.
